price_note: Prices reflect the heavily fluctuating 2023-2024 sub-market realities and distribution shortages, where informal open-market prices frequently crossed 10,000 ETB per quintal (100 kg = two 50 kg bags). Ranges are indicative only.
source_documents: EthioSIS Soil Fertility Status and Fertilizer Recommendation Atlas (FDRE Ministry of Agriculture + ATA/ATI)
Integrated Soil Fertility Management (ISFM) Technical Manual (FDRE Ministry of Agriculture)
Ethiopian Fertilizer and Soil Health Roadmap (2026-2035)

products.name: Nitrogen-Phosphate-Sulfur
products.label: NPS (19% N, 38% P2O5, 7% S)
products.formulator: OCP Group Morocco — blend formulated for East Africa to close the sulfur deficiencies uncovered by EthioSIS

application.method: Apply at planting; broadcast with immediate soil incorporation
restrictions: Never broadcast onto the surface without immediate incorporation — the ammonium-N component volatilizes
Do not apply during the dry season or under moisture stress; soil moisture is required to dissolve the phosphate complex

decision_rules: Soil test S < 20 ppm with B > 0.5 ppm (boron sufficient) → select NPS over DAP
Preferred basal P source wherever EthioSIS maps show sulfur deficiency

products.name: Nitrogen-Phosphate-Sulfur-Boron
products.label: NPSB (18.5% N, 36.9% P2O5, 6.8% S, 0.4% B)
products.formulator: Regional blends — base NPS (95 kg) + Borax (~4.9 kg) yields roughly 18.1N-36.1P2O5-6.7S-0.71B

application.method: Strictly basal; uniform field broadcast or precise row placement
restrictions: Micronutrient toxicity warning: high local boron concentrations cause localized seedling burn and phytotoxicity
Ensure uniform blending/broadcast — never concentrate granules at one spot

decision_rules: EthioSIS atlas grid marks boron deficiency (common across Amhara and Southern Ethiopian clay soils) → NPSB
B-deficient soils such as Gubalafto and Dawuro

products.name: Urea
products.label: Urea (46% N)

application.method: Split application: 1/3 at planting, 2/3 at the critical vegetative phase
restrictions: Never leave on an exposed dry soil surface — volatilization can strip up to 40% of the nitrogen within 48 hours unless incorporated by rainfall, irrigation, or soil cover
Do not apply during heavy downpours to prevent nitrate leaching
Top-dress at knee-high for maize, 30-40 days after sowing for teff

decision_rules: Mandatory accompaniment to basal fertilizers (NPS/NPSB) for high nitrogen-demand crops like maize and wheat

products.name: Di-Ammonium Phosphate
products.label: DAP (18% N, 46% P2O5)

application.method: Basal placement in the seed furrow
restrictions: Phased out for macro-use by the MoA since 2014-2015 to prevent sulfur starvation
Only recommend when targeted soils have optimal sulfur/micronutrient counts or blended fertilizers face regional supply-chain blockages

decision_rules: Exception use in flooded/acidic lowland systems (e.g., Fogera rice plains, sugarcane) where alternative dynamics occur
Not for general use while NPS/NPSB supply is available

products.name: Region-Specific Blends (Formula 3 / Formula 5)
products.label: Region blend (13.4% N, 26.8% P2O5, 14.1% K2O, 5.4% S, 1.7% Zn, 0.5% B)
products.formulator: Region-specific blended formulas adding potassium (standard example: 13.7N-27.4P2O5-14.4K2O-5.1S-0.54B)

application.method: Apply directly into planting furrows for deep-root stimulation
restrictions: Avoid highly alkaline soils of the Rift Valley unless specialized acidic modifiers are present
Best placed in the furrow, not broadcast

decision_rules: Potassium-deficient areas where decades of heavy rainfall leached exchangeable K (Gojjam, Gamo, Sidama)
Tuber crops (potato, cassava), enset, and perennial fruits (avocado, mango) in the western and southwestern highlands
